Document: Part 82 – Closed material procedure
Part 2 of 2
==================================================
## Application for a declaration

## 82.22

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.22] (1) An application under section 6(2) of the Act for a declaration must be made by the applicant filing with the court—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.22] (a) a statement of reasons to support the application and any additional written submissions;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.22] (b) material in relation to which the court is asked to find that the first condition in section 6 of the Act is met;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.22] (c) the details of any special advocate already appointed under rule 82.9 (appointment of a special advocate). [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.22] (2) Where the applicant is the Secretary of State, the statement of reasons required by paragraph (1)(a) must include the Secretary of State’s reasons for not making, or not advising another person to make, a claim for public interest immunity in relation to the material on which the application would be based. ## Directions for hearing of an application

## 82.23

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (1) When a party to relevant civil proceedings or (if the Secretary of State is not a party) the Secretary of State makes an application under section 6(2) of the Act for a declaration, the court must serve notice of the application on—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (a) all other parties and (if the Secretary of State is neither a party nor the applicant) the Secretary of State;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (b) the legal representatives of all other parties and (where relevant) the Secretary of State; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (c) the special advocate,

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] and must give directions for a directions hearing unless it considers that the application can be determined on the papers, in which case it must give directions as it considers appropriate. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (1A) If the court considers that it is necessary before it can determine whether to make a declaration under section 6(2) of the Act, it may, on application or of its own motion, direct the relevant person to file—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (a) a draft response document, addressing the matters directed by the court (“a draft closed summary”); or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (b) having first considered whether a draft closed summary is sufficient to determine the matter, a defence or response, as appropriate, to one or more of the grounds identified in the claim, together with such further directions as to its content as the court considers appropriate (“a draft closed defence”);

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (1B) A draft closed summary or a draft closed defence—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (a)shall be disclosed to—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (i)the court;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (ii)any person appointed as a special advocate; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (iii)where the Secretary of State is not the relevant person but is a party to the proceedings, the Secretary of State,

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] but must not be disclosed otherwise; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (b)shall not be relied upon other than in determining whether to make a declaration under section 6(2) of the Act. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (1C) A draft closed defence is not a statement of case. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (2) At the directions hearing the court must give directions—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (a) for the hearing of the application; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (b) specifying a date and time by which the parties and the special advocate must file and serve any written evidence or written submissions. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.23] (Rule 82.6 makes provision for hearings to be conducted in private.)

## Notification by applicant following hearing of application

## 82.24

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.24] (1) When the court has determined an application made under section 6(2) of the Act, the applicant must within 7 days of that determination serve written notice of the outcome of the application on every other party to the proceedings and (if the Secretary of State is not a party) on the Secretary of State. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.24] (2) The notice must be limited to stating whether the application was granted or refused. ## Secretary of State to be joined where declaration made

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Secretary of State to be joined where declaration made] 82.25 If the court makes a declaration under section 6 of the Act and the Secretary of State is not already a party to the proceedings in relation to which the declaration is made, the court must order the Secretary of State to be joined as a party to those proceedings, unless the Secretary of State does not wish to be joined and notifies the court in writing accordingly. ## Directions following declaration

## 82.26

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.26] (1) If the court makes a declaration under section 6 of the Act, it must give directions for the further management of the case, or for a directions hearing, or for both. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.26] (2) The court must, either when giving directions under paragraph (1) or at the directions hearing (if it directs such a hearing), give directions—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.26] (a) for a hearing of a closed material application; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.26] (b) specifying a date and time by which the parties and special advocate must file and serve any written evidence or written submissions, unless it considers that the application can be determined on the papers, in which case it must give directions as it considers appropriate. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.26] (3) Directions given under this rule may include directions for—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.26] (a) the filing by any party of—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.26] (i) a statement of case; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.26] (ii) an amended statement of case; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.26] (b) a hearing of a closed material application in relation to such a statement of case. ## IV REVIEW AND REVOCATION OF THE DECLARATIONS MADE UNDER SECTION 6 OF THE ACT

## Scope of this section

## 82.27 This section contains rules about—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.27 This section contains rules about—] (a) revocation—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.27 This section contains rules about—] (i) of the court’s own motion; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.27 This section contains rules about—] (ii) on application, of a declaration made under section 6 of the Act; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.27 This section contains rules about—] (b) the court’s formal review of such a declaration. ## Possible revocation of declaration: court’s own motion

## 82.28

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.28] (1) This rule applies if the court at any time considers that a declaration made under section 6 of the Act may no longer be in the interests of the fair and effective administration of justice in the proceedings. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.28] (2) The court must in writing—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.28] (a) notify the parties (and the Secretary of State if not a party) and the special advocate that it is considering whether to revoke the declaration; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.28] (b) invite them to make submissions. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.28] (3) Each party (and the Secretary of State if not a party) and the special advocate must within 28 days of the date of notification under paragraph

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.28] (2) file a response either—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.28] (a) containing written submissions supporting or opposing revocation of the declaration and giving reasons; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.28] (b) confirming that the party (or the Secretary of State, or the special advocate, as appropriate) does not wish to make any submissions. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.28] (4) The court may, on receipt of the responses under paragraph (3), either—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.28] (a) give directions—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.28] (i) for a hearing to determine whether the declaration should be revoked; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.28] (ii) specifying a date and time by which the parties (and Secretary of State if not a party) and special advocate must file and serve any written evidence or written submissions; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.28] (b) determine the issue without a hearing. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.28] (5) A hearing under this rule shall take place in the absence of the specially represented party and the specially represented party’s legal representative. ## Application for revocation of declaration

## 82.29

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.29] (1) An application under section 7(4)(a) of the Act for revocation of a declaration made under section 6 of the Act must be made by the applicant filing with the court—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.29] (a) a statement of reasons to support the application; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.29] (b) any written submissions. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.29] (2) When such an application has been made, the court must serve notice of the application on—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.29] (a) all other parties and (if the Secretary of State is neither a party nor the applicant) the Secretary of State;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.29] (b) the legal representatives of those parties and (where relevant) the Secretary of State; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.29] (c) the special advocate, and must give directions for a hearing unless it considers that the application can be determined on the papers, in which case it may give directions as it considers appropriate. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.29] (3) Each party (and the Secretary of State if neither a party nor the applicant) and the special advocate must within 28 days of the date of notification under paragraph (2) file a response either—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.29] (a) containing written submissions supporting or opposing revocation of the declaration and giving reasons; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.29] (b) confirming that the party (or the Secretary of State, or the special advocate, as appropriate) does not wish to make any submissions. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.29] (4) The court must, after receipt of the responses under paragraph (3), either—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.29] (a) give directions—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.29] (i) for a hearing to determine whether the declaration should be revoked; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.29] (ii) specifying a date and time by which the parties (and Secretary of State if not a party) and special advocate must file and serve any written evidence or written submissions; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.29] (b) determine the issue without a hearing. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.29] (5) A hearing under this rule shall take place in the absence of the specially represented party and the specially represented party’s legal representative. ## Review of declaration: formal review

## 82.30

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.30] (1) Once the pre-trial disclosure exercise in proceedings where there has been a declaration under section 6 of the Act has been completed, the court must review whether the declaration continues to be in the interests of the fair and effective administration of justice in the proceedings. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.30] (2) If the court considers that the declaration may no longer be in the interests of the fair and effective administration of justice in the proceedings, it must proceed in accordance with paragraphs (2) to (5) of rule 82.28. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.30] (3) If the court considers that the declaration continues to be in the interests of the fair and effective administration of justice in the proceedings, it may so declare without a hearing. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.30] (4) For the purposes of section 7(3) of the Act and this rule, the pre-trial disclosure exercise in the proceedings is to be considered to have been completed—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.30] (a) where the claim is one to which rule 31.5(2) does not apply, when disclosure equivalent to standard disclosure has been completed in accordance with this Part;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.30] (b) where the claim is one to which rule 31.5(2) applies, when disclosure equivalent to that directed under rule 31.5(7) and (8) has been completed in accordance with this Part. ## V REVIEW, UNDER SECTION 18 OF THE ACT, OF A CERTIFICATE UNDER SECTION 17(3)(e) OF THE ACT

## Review of certification

## 82.31

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (1) An application under section 18(1) of the Act to have a certificate issued under section 17(3)(e) of the Act set aside must be made by the applicant filing with the court—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (a) a statement of reasons to support the application; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (b) any written submissions. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (2) The court with which the documents in paragraph (1)(a) and (b) must be filed is—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (a) the High Court, if the court seised of the proceedings in relation to which the certificate was issued is the High Court or the County Court; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (b) the Court of Appeal, if the court seised of the proceedings in relation to which the certificate was issued is the Court of Appeal. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (3) When such an application has been made, the court must serve notice of the application on the Secretary of State and the Secretary of State’s legal representative, and on the special advocate when a special advocate has been appointed pursuant to rule 82.9. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (4) The Secretary of State must, within 28 days of the date of notification under paragraph (3), file, and serve upon the special advocate, a response either—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (a) containing written submissions opposing the setting aside of the certificate and giving reasons; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (b) confirming that the Secretary of State does not oppose the setting aside of the certificate. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (5) The special advocate must within 28 days of being served under paragraph (4) file, and serve on the Secretary of State, a response either—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (a) containing written submissions supporting the setting aside of the certificate and giving reasons; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (b) confirming that the special advocate does not wish to make any submissions. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (6) The court must, after receipt of the responses under paragraphs (4) and (5), either—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (a) give directions—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (i) for a hearing to determine whether the certificate should be revoked; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (ii) specifying a date and time by which the parties (and the Secretary of State if not a party) and special advocate must file and serve any written evidence or written submissions; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (b) determine the issue without a hearing. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.31] (7) A hearing under this rule shall take place in the absence of the specially represented party and the specially represented party’s legal representative. ## VI APPEALS TO THE COURT OF APPEAL

## Modification of Part 52 (appeals)

## 82.32

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.32] (1) Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.32] (a) against an order of the High Court on or in relation to an application under section 6(2), 7(4) or 18(1) of the Act, or section 6 proceedings;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.32] (b) where the order under appeal was not made on or in relation to a matter within sub-paragraph (a) but the appeal proceedings involve such a matter or are section 6 proceedings. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.32] (2) Paragraph (1) is subject to—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.32] (a) rule 82.2;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.32] (b) Section 2 of this Part; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.32] (c) paragraph (3) of this rule. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.32] (3) The appellant must serve a copy of the appellant’s notice on any special advocate.
